source: ARMGDDN App native edition (hand written; sections 12 and 13 carried over from the website Wiki)

sections.title: 1. What ARMGDDN App Is
sections.html: ARMGDDN App is one app for finding and downloading everything in the ARMGDDN library: PC games, PCVR games, Testing, 3D printer models, Pirated PC apps, Comics and Music. You browse, pick, and press Download. The app downloads in the background and keeps going while you do something else. There is no separate website to open and no second app: browsing and downloading are the same window.

sections.title: 2. Getting Started
sections.html:
2.1 Install

Download ARMGDDN App for Windows, Linux or macOS 13 or newer from armgddnbrowser.com. Run it once so it can finish setting itself up.

2.2 Log in

Sign in with Telegram when the app asks, and approve the login there. You stay logged in on that computer.

2.3 First look

The window opens on Home. Everything else is one click away in the bar across the top. Linux and Steam Deck players: see section 13.

sections.title: 3. Finding Your Way Around
sections.html:
3.1 The top bar

Home, PC Games, PCVR Games, Testing, 3D Printer Models, Pirated PC Apps, Comics and Music are on the left. Tools, Settings, Wiki, My List, Requests and Downloads are on the right. The page you are on is highlighted.

3.2 The second bar

Each page has its own controls here: a Back button, the page name, then search, category, sort and so on where they apply.

3.3 Back

Every screen has a Back button. Alt+Left and your mouse's back button work too.

3.4 Grid or list

The Grid / List switch on the right of the second bar shows titles as cards with art, or as a plain list. The app remembers your choice.

3.5 The A-Z bar

On long lists, the letter strip at the side shows only the titles that start with that letter. Click the letter again to bring the whole list back.

sections.title: 4. Home
sections.html:
• Trending. The strip of what's being downloaded most right now (7 and 30 days). Click a title to open it.
  • Game Radar. Picks chosen from what you opened, saved and downloaded. Refresh for new ones, dismiss any you don't want, reset to bring them back.
  • Resume. Takes you back to the folder you were in last time.

sections.title: 5. Browsing and Searching
sections.html:
• Open a section from the top bar. If a section has only one folder inside, the app opens it for you. A section whose download quota is used up is dimmed and can't be opened; quota usually resets within 24 hours.
  • Folders that point elsewhere. A game folder that is almost empty is only a pointer to the other server. It says "You must download from PCVR server" (or PC server) with a Go there button that takes you to the right section.
  • Search filters the page you are on. Punctuation and spacing are ignored, so "spider man" finds "Spider-Man".
  • Search everywhere. Tick Search everywhere to search every section at once.
  • Mistyped a name? If nothing matches exactly, the app shows the closest titles ("No exact match, closest:"). It forgives one slip in each word of five or more letters.
  • Also in another section. When you search inside one section and the same title is in another (a newer build in Testing, for example), a line under the search says so, with a Search all sections button.
  • Newest and Older. When the same game is in more than one place with different builds, the results are tagged Newest or Older so you don't have to compare version numbers.
  • Tell me when it is added. Under any search, this button puts the title on your watchlist. You get a Telegram message when it is added to the library, or when a newer build of it appears. My watchlist shows what you're watching, and you can stop watching any title there. It is the same list the website uses.
  • Category / genre. Where a section has them, the dropdown narrows the list (for example Music genres). Choose No genre to see titles not yet tagged.
  • Sort by Name, Popularity, Added or Released, and press the reverse button to flip the order.
  • Export list. Saves the section's titles and sizes as a file you can open in Excel.

sections.title: 6. A Game's Page
sections.html:
Click a title for its details: the cover, Watch trailer, Read README, Browse files, Add to My List and Download.

  • Art. Titles show their cover. Where a title has none yet, it shows its category's art until real art is added.
  • README. Some games show their README before downloading.
  • Browse files. Look inside a game's folder and download single files.

sections.title: 7. Downloading
sections.html:
7.1 Start

Press Download on a game, album, comic collection or 3D model. The download starts straight away.

7.2 Several at once

Tick Pick several items, tick the titles you want, and download them together.

7.3 Update patches

If a game has an Update Patch, the app asks whether you already have the old repack. Yes downloads only the patch, No downloads only the full repack, Cancel stops.

7.4 The Downloads page

Shows every download with its progress, speed and time left. Each has Pause, Resume, Cancel or Retry, and Open folder when it's done. Clear history removes finished ones from the list.

7.5 Updating a game you already have

In Settings, Your games, Check my games lists which of your downloaded games have a newer version. Click one to open it in the library.

sections.title: 8. Music and Comics
sections.html:
• Music is by artist and album. The genre dropdown narrows the list.
  • Comics are by series and issue. Where a comic's details have been checked, it shows under its proper title with its issue number and release date, and series are listed in release order. A ComicVine tag next to it opens that issue on ComicVine.
  • Publisher collections. At the top of the Comics page, just under the Komga box, each publisher's collection (Marvel, DC and more as they are added) has a Download All button that downloads every series of it that has been copied so far.
  • Only what I'm missing. Already have part of the collection? In Tools, scan your Comics or Music folder; the app then shows what you don't have.
  • Komga. The Comics page has a Komga box with links to install it (section 12).
  • Folders. Where Comics and Music download is set in Settings, Folders.

sections.title: 9. My List and Requests
sections.html:
• My List holds what you saved for later. Press the heart on any card.
  • Requests. Ask for a game that isn't in the library, and read the replies. When requests are closed, the page says so.

sections.title: 10. Settings
sections.html:
Settings is in groups, one card each.

  • Updates: Check for updates (turns into Update to vX when there is one), What's New, Update automatically.
  • Folders: Download, Comics and Music folders.
  • Downloads: how many at the same time, connections per file (leave on Automatic), speed limit, check files after downloading, extract .7z files automatically, the video on opening .7z files, and the download schedule (pause or slow downloads at set times).
  • Your games: Check my games.
  • The app and its window: notifications, the Minimize button hiding the window to the tray, the Close button keeping the app running in the tray (off: closing quits the app), start with the computer, start minimized, and the login animation.
  • Import: bring over the settings of an earlier ARMGDDN App install, or your website preferences (My List, theme, hidden sections, recent searches).
  • Help and reports: send error reports, and Help with problems (section 11).

sections.title: 11. Updates, Problems and Help
sections.html:
11.1 Updates

The app checks once an hour. When there is a new version a bar appears under the header with Update now. You can also press File > Check for updates. If downloads are running, finish or pause them first, because updating restarts the app.

11.2 What's New

Settings, Updates, Show what's new.

11.3 Help with problems

Settings, Help and reports: run a check, test your connection speed, copy a report, or send your log to the chat. Help > Open the log folder opens the log files.

11.4 Exit

File > Exit closes the app completely. Closing the window may keep it running in the tray, depending on your setting.

sections.title: 12. Reading Comics with Komga
sections.html:
Komga is a free comic server and reader. It reads the comics you download from the Comics collection, builds a library with covers, series and reading progress, and lets you read in a browser or on your phone. You run Komga yourself; ARMGDDN does not host it. On the Comics page, the Download Komga row at the top takes you to Komga's own official install page. Below it are reading-order rows (see 14.4).

12.1 Before you start

  • Download with App works for comics exactly as it does for games. Use a folder you will keep for comics, for example D:\Comics, and not a game folder.
  • Comics arrive as .cbz and .cbr files. ARMGDDN App never unpacks these (it only extracts .7z), so leave them as they are. Komga reads them directly.
  • Downloads keep the library's folder layout: a collection folder (for example Batman Collection) holds one folder per series, and each series folder holds its issues. Download one series, one whole collection, or several collections at once. A download that spans several collections is saved in a folder called Comics, with a folder per collection inside it.

12.2 Get and install Komga

  1. Click Download Komga at the top of the Comics page, or go to komga.org and open the Installation section.
  2. Pick the method that suits you: the Desktop app (Windows and macOS, updates itself), the Microsoft Store, Docker, or the jar file (needs Java 17 or newer). If you are not sure, use the Desktop app.
  3. Open Komga in your browser (by default http://localhost:25600) and create your admin account.

12.3 Add your comics

  1. In Komga, open Libraries and choose Add library.
  2. Name it Comics and set the root folder to the folder you download comics into.
  3. Leave the options on their defaults and save. Komga scans and builds your library.
  4. Each series folder becomes a series in Komga. A collection folder such as Batman Collection only groups its series and is not a series itself. If a comic has a ComicInfo.xml inside, Komga uses its title, number and summary.

12.4 Reading orders (Add to My Komga)

Under the Komga row on the Comics page are complete reading orders for Marvel, DC, Batman, Daredevil, Spider-Man and Superman. Each one can be added to your own Komga as a read list.

  1. In Komga open Account Settings, then API Keys, and add a key.
  2. On the Comics page click Add reading orders in the Komga box (or open Tools) and choose the list you want.
  3. The first time, enter your Komga address (usually http://localhost:25600) and the key in Tools. They stay on your PC.

Make sure comics are in Komga before you generate a read list or they won't show up. You can always generate another. Adding a list again replaces the one you already have with the fresh version.

New reading orders appear on this page by themselves when a comic collection grows past 40 issues, or when a list is added.

12.5 Only what I'm missing

If you already have part of the collection, you do not need to download it again. Open Tools in the top bar, use the Comics scan and choose the folder your comics are in. ARMGDDN App reads that folder on your PC (nothing about it is sent to the site), compares it with the library, and shows how many comics you have and how many are missing.

  1. On the Comics page, click Only what I'm missing next to a reading order. You can also pick the whole library or any list in Tools.
  2. Click Download what I'm missing. Only the comics you do not have are downloaded, straight into your comics folder with the library's own folder layout.

Comics are matched by the Comic Vine number inside each file, then by series, issue number and year. A cut-short or empty file is flagged as damaged and is downloaded again. Your own files are never unpacked or changed.

Music works the same way: see section 8, or scan your Music folder in Tools. Every artist, album, collection and series folder also has its own Only what I'm missing button, which compares just that folder.

Scan is slow or won't start. The scan first matches your files to the library by name and size, so most of a collection is recognised without being opened. If it says the scan did not start, you have been signed out: press Only what I'm missing on the site, then scan again. If it is still slow, run Check my setup. A comics folder on a cloud or network drive reads slowly, and the report will say so. A local copy is much faster. Update ARMGDDN App to the latest version for the faster scan and the sign-in fix.

12.6 Adding more later

Download new issues into the same series folder. Komga rescans on its own schedule, or open the library menu and choose Scan library files. If a series looks wrong, check that the issues are all in one folder and that the files were not renamed.

12.7 Reading on your phone

Komga works in any browser. Many comic apps also connect to it (look for apps that support Komga or OPDS). Sign in with the same address and account as the web page.

12.8 Troubleshooting

  • Nothing shows up: check the library's root folder is the folder you downloaded into, then run Scan library files.
  • No cover or a wrong cover: this usually means the first page is not a normal image. Open the book in Komga and set a cover from its pages.
  • A .cbr will not open: the file may be damaged. Try downloading it again, and tell Old Man of the Hills if it keeps happening.
  • These collections are still in the very early stages and some series are incomplete. If you can help fill gaps, or have content to donate, please contact Old Man of the Hills.

sections.title: 13. Installing Games on Linux (Faugus)
sections.html:
This section is for Linux and Steam Deck players. ARMGDDN does not officially support Linux for its repacks. This is a method you can try, using Faugus Launcher, which runs every Windows game through Proton, with one separate Wine prefix per game. Everything after the extraction step happens inside the launcher. Windows players can skip this section. Guide by Ifudgedup W.

ARMGDDN App downloads the files the same way on Linux (see section 2). This section starts once the download has finished.

13.1 The whole recipe

  1. Check the game on ProtonDB. Is it worth it under Proton? (15.2)
  2. Install Faugus. Flatpak, PPA, Copr or AUR, one time. (15.3)
  3. Download a Proton build in Proton Manager. GE-Proton or Proton-CachyOS. (15.4)
  4. Extract the repack. Keep all the parts in one folder and extract the first part. (15.5)
  5. Press + in Faugus, choose Game/App and fill in Title, Prefix and Specific Proton. (15.6)
  6. Use Run an installer and pick setup.exe, all from inside Faugus. (15.6 and 15.7)
  7. Pick the game's .exe in the same dialog, then press Play. (15.8 and 15.9)

If a repack's installer works under Proton, there is nothing else to copy over or patch by hand.

13.2 Step 1: Check ProtonDB before you download

Five minutes on protondb.com can save you a six-hour download. ProtonDB is the community database of how Windows games run under Proton, the same technology Faugus uses, so a game's verdict there applies to your copy too.

Read the tier badge, best to worst: Native (has a Linux version), Platinum (works out of the box), Gold (small tweaks), Silver (needs tinkering), Bronze (painful), Borked (does not run).

  • Gold or Platinum: download with confidence.
  • Silver: go ahead, but expect to tune it.
  • Borked: do not bother. No launcher can fix what Proton itself cannot run.
  • Scroll the reports and copy what works. The best reports list the exact "Tinker Steps" and launch options. If players get a game running with a specific Proton build, use the same one in 15.4 and 15.6, and the same launch options in 15.11.

Note: ProtonDB reports assume Steam. Ignore anything about anti-cheat or online modes. The single-player result is what carries over to ARMGDDN games.

13.3 Step 2: Install Faugus (one time)

Pick the block for your system and run it in a terminal.

Flatpak (any distro, including Steam Deck):
flatpak install flathub io.github.Faugus.faugus-launcher

Ubuntu / Linux Mint:
sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:faugus/faugus-launcher
sudo apt update && sudo apt install faugus-launcher

Fedora / Nobara:
sudo dnf copr enable faugus/faugus-launcher
sudo dnf install faugus-launcher

Arch:
yay -S faugus-launcher

Steam Deck: switch to Desktop Mode and run the Flatpak command. The launcher then appears in Discover under Installed.

Stay at the keyboard: each of these commands will stop and ask you to confirm. Read what it is about to install, then answer the prompt yourself (Y to continue, N to stop). Never add -y, --yes or --noconfirm to skip the questions.

13.4 Step 3: Download a Proton build (one time)

Click the gear icon in the bottom bar, open Proton Manager, choose a build and click Download on the newest dated one. Then set it as your Default Proton in the General settings.

Choose between GE-Proton and Proton-CachyOS in the dropdown. If ProtonDB recommended a specific build for your game, pick that one.

13.5 Step 4: Extract the repack

This is the only step outside the launcher. ARMGDDN games arrive as split archives. Keep all the parts together in one folder, then extract the first part with your archive manager or from a terminal:

7z x "game.part1.rar"
If you do not have it yet: sudo apt install p7zip-rar p7zip-full

  • The result is a folder containing setup.exe (or install.exe).
  • Never run the installer from inside the archive viewer. It fails silently.
  • Keep the folder path plain: ordinary English letters and no spaces.

13.6 Step 5: Add the game and run the installer inside Faugus

Click + (bottom left), open the Game/App tab and fill it in:

  • Type: Windows Game.
  • Title: the game's name. This also names its prefix folder.
  • Prefix: leave the automatic value (~/Faugus/<game>).
  • Path: use the magnifier or menu button, choose Run an installer and browse to setup.exe. The file picker is inside Faugus.
  • Tick Specific Proton and pick the build from 15.4, or the one ProtonDB recommended.

Click Ok. The repack installer opens in its own fresh prefix. The Add Game window stays open. Do not close it. You finish it in 15.8.

13.7 Step 6: Let the installer do its thing

It is a normal repack installer running under Proton. Five rules:

  • Untick the "system requirements check" if it is offered. Proton reports odd hardware.
  • Keep the default install location. It lands inside the prefix, exactly where the next step expects it.
  • The long "decompressing" bar is normal. Do not close it.
  • Untick "launch game when finished". Launch from Faugus instead.
  • Decline any optional bundled software, such as browsers or "hubs".

13.8 Step 7: Point the entry at the game's .exe

Go back to the Add Game window, which is still open. No file manager is needed.

  • Use the Path magnifier, choose Select an executable and browse to ~/Faugus/<game>/drive_c/Program Files/<Game>/<game>.exe. The picker starts where the installer ran.
  • Tick Shortcut for Desktop, App Menu or Steam, as you like, and click Ok.

The game now lives in Faugus's list for good. Faugus can also create shortcuts from the installer by itself, but picking the .exe directly is the reliable way, because installers sometimes pick stubs or launchers.

13.9 Step 8: Play

Select the game and press the Play button at the bottom right. The first launch is slower while the prefix warms up. The bottom bar holds: add, settings, search, a skull button that stops a running game, and Play. Sort and filter chips are at the top. With a gamepad, L1 adds a game and Triangle opens the game menu.

13.10 Step 9: Tuning and fixing, if needed

Open the game's entry again and go to the Tools tab.

  • Launch Settings holds per-game environment variables built from ready-made presets, for example VKD3D_CONFIG=no_upload_hvw, game-performance, WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8" for older games, and a gamescope resolution line. There are also Pre- and Post-launch scripts.
  • Game Arguments takes things like -fullscreen. Winetricks installs Visual C++ and .NET. Run runs any .exe inside the prefix.
  • If you see a DLL error, run the matching installer from the release's _Redist folder using Tools, then Run (DirectX and the Visual C++ redistributables), or use Winetricks.
  • ProtonDB's reported launch options go in Launch Settings. Leave out the %command% wrapper, because Faugus adds it.

13.11 Troubleshooting

  • The game is Borked on ProtonDB: no launcher fixes that. Try another game or a different release.
  • The installer window flashes and closes: you ran it from inside the archive viewer, or a .part file is missing. Extract everything first (15.5).
  • A DLL is missing (xinput1_3, d3dcompiler_47, mfc140 and so on): Tools, then Run, the matching installer from the release's _Redist folder, or install it with Winetricks.
  • Black screen or crash on launch: switch "Specific Proton" between GE-Proton and Proton-CachyOS, or try the exact build ProtonDB's reports mention.
  • "Not enough space" in the installer: free up space where the prefix lives, or change Settings, then General, then Default Prefixes Location.
  • Steam shortcuts are greyed out or you see "No Steam Users Found": this is the Flatpak sandbox. Apply the Flatpak override commands from the Faugus repository's README.
  • Where is everything? Prefixes live in the Default Prefixes Location (~/Faugus by default). Proton builds live in ~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/.

Useful links: protondb.com, the Faugus Launcher page on GitHub (github.com/Faugus/faugus-launcher) and on Flathub (faugus-launcher).

sections.title: 14. FAQ
sections.html:
• Do I still need the Companion? No. ARMGDDN App is both.
  • Is there an old window to go back to? No. Since version 6.0.0 this is the only window, and it does everything the website and the old Companion did.
  • Where are my downloads? Settings, Folders. Open folder on the Downloads page takes you there.
  • A page froze or shows an error. Press Try again or Back. It is written to the log, and Help with problems can send it.
  • Where is the admin panel? On the website, for staff.
